methods.note: Task assignment algorithm (Algorithm-1) relies on genetic algorithm with unspecified hyperparameters (population size Np, iteration count iter, tournament size k, crossover probability ρc, mutation probability ρm). No convergence proof, termination criteria, or computational complexity analysis provided. Genetic algorithm fitness function defined in equation (13) but no justification for absolute error as optimization objective. Paper claims algorithm assigns tasks to maintain thermal balance but does not prove optimality or compare against baseline heuristics.

code.note: No source code, simulation scripts, or supplementary materials provided. Integration between GEM5, McPAT, HotSpot simulators, and Algorithm-1 is described qualitatively but not documented in executable form. Pseudo-code in Algorithm-1 uses notation (⊙ for element-wise multiplication) without formal definition. No reproducibility artifacts (git repository, Docker container, configuration files) linked or available.

parameters.note: Table 1 MiBench section lists 10 benchmark tasks but text Section 5.2 claims only 6 MiBench tasks. Total benchmark count stated as 20 but MiBench label inconsistency creates ambiguity. Thermal RC-model parameters R and C are completely absent—equations (1) and (2) cannot be evaluated without these values. Genetic algorithm parameters (Np, iter, k, ρc, ρm) referenced in Algorithm-1 line 5 are not given numerical values anywhere in paper. Initial temperatures Case 2 show four different core values (65.48°C, 49.77°C, 45.82°C, 51.86°C) but origin and justification for these specific values not explained.

config.note: GEM5 simulator configuration not documented: no gem5 version, CPU model specification, cache hierarchy configuration, memory controller type beyond label 'DDRx1', instruction set, or compilation flags. McPAT simulator configuration absent: no architecture XML template, power model file, version, or parameter extraction method described. HotSpot simulator completely unconfigured: no floorplan file (.flp) provided, no thermal model (.model) specified, no solver settings (transient vs. steady-state, time step, convergence tolerance), no die size or block dimensions. Figure 6 shows abstract architecture diagram but contains no geometric coordinates, die dimensions, or spatial layout for HotSpot. Task assignment algorithm hyperparameters unset: decision factor curve (Figure 3) is plotted but equation (10) uses T_max as only reference—no justification for parabolic shape or derivation from thermal principles.

data.note: Table 1 provides 20 benchmark task parameters (execution time, leakage power, dynamic power, energy) but energy values appear inconsistent with stated formula Eni = Pi * ti. For example, task_401_bzip2: stated energy 123.106 mJ but (1.15327 + 0.318345) W × 0.083654 s ≈ 124.4 mJ (small discrepancy but suggests rounding or different power definition). Task energy calculated from dynamic power alone yields different results: 0.318345 W × 0.083654 s ≈ 26.6 mJ, not matching table. Paper claims energy from Pi (average power) but table splits leakage and dynamic power. Clarification on which power component (dynamic, leakage, or total) is Pi in equations is missing. No raw GEM5 statistics files, McPAT output logs, or HotSpot trace files provided to verify benchmark measurements.

findings.reason: Equations (1) and (2) defining thermal transient behavior depend on thermal resistance R (K/W) and thermal capacitance C (J/K) which are never specified numerically. Paper states these are 'parameters' but provides no values, lookup tables, derivations from physical die properties, or references to manufacturer datasheets. Without R and C, the core temperature evolution equations cannot be evaluated.
findings.locator: Section 2 Theoretical Background, Equations (1)-(2), pages 3-4; unresolved across entire paper

findings.reason: Algorithm-1 line 5 lists inputs 'Np, iter, n, k, ρc, ρm' as genetic algorithm configuration but none of these are assigned values in paper. Np (population size), iter (iteration count), k (tournament size), ρc (crossover probability), ρm (mutation probability) are essential to reproduce the algorithm yet remain undefined. Section 5.3 simulation results do not report which parameter values were used.
findings.locator: Section 4 Algorithm-1, page 7; Section 5.1-5.3 Simulation setup and results pages 7-10 make no mention of these values

findings.reason: Section 5.2 Task benchmarks text states 'Mibench' group but Table 1 MiBench section lists 10 task rows (basicmath, bitcount, qsort, susan, patricia, sha, blowfish, pgp, tiff2bw, typeset) while introductory text in Section 2 and abstract claim 6 MiBench tasks. Total benchmark count stated as 20 implies 5 Spec2006 + 6 MiBench + 9 MediaBench = 20, but Table 1 shows 5 + 10 + 5 = 20 with MiBench over-counted.
findings.locator: Section 5.2 page 8, Table 1 pages 8; Section 2 Introduction page 2 references 'Mibench [28]' generically

findings.reason: Paper Section 3.2 states 'Eni could be achieved by multiplying Pi and ti together to determine the energy of each Task' where Pi is defined as 'average power'. Table 1 provides both 'Leakage Power' and 'Dynamic Power' columns but unclear which represents Pi or if Pi = Leakage + Dynamic. Checking task_401_bzip2: (0.318345 W dynamic + 1.15327 W leakage) × 0.083654 s = 123.1 mJ matches table, but formula derivation for split power components not explained. No statement of whether energy is computed from GEM5+McPAT product or extracted independently from power tables.
findings.locator: Section 3.2 page 4; Table 1 page 8; discrepancy suggests Pi includes both leakage and dynamic but this is inferred, not stated

findings.reason: Paper mentions 'simulated by a hotspot simulator' (Section 4, page 7) to compute core temperatures but provides no HotSpot configuration: no version number, no floorplan file (.flp) with die geometry or block coordinates, no thermal model file (.model), no solver method (transient vs. steady-state), no time step, no convergence criteria. Figure 6 shows abstract quad-core architecture without coordinates or dimensions required for HotSpot .flp format.
findings.locator: Section 4 page 6-7; Section 5.1 Figure 6 page 7; Section 5.3 Simulation results page 9 invoke HotSpot without configuration details

findings.reason: Section 3.2 states 'ti is the execution time of Taski could be accurately measured in selected CPU configuration by GEM5 [24]' but no GEM5 version, configuration command-line options, CPU model parameters (ISA, pipeline depth, branch predictor), cache hierarchy setup beyond label, memory controller type, or output statistics files documented. No reference to gem5 manual, published papers on methodology, or reproducible script provided.
findings.locator: Section 3.2 page 4; Reference [24] cited but GEM5 configuration details absent throughout paper

findings.reason: Section 3.2 claims 'Pi is could be measured using multicore power, area, and timing (McPAT) [25] with the same CPU configuration that was used for GEM5' but no McPAT version, architecture XML definition file, power model template, thermal model parameters, or extraction methodology documented. McPAT requires detailed architecture specification files (.xml) not provided or described.
findings.locator: Section 3.2 page 4; Reference [25] cited but McPAT configuration details absent throughout paper

findings.reason: Section 5.3.2 Different initial temperature case assigns arbitrary core temperatures (65.48°C, 49.77°C, 45.82°C, 51.86°C) but no explanation for why these specific values were chosen, how they represent realistic thermal imbalance scenarios, or whether they are derived from prior simulation or measurement. No justification provided for case selection or representativeness.
findings.locator: Section 5.3.2 page 9-10: 'Core1 Temp: 65.48 ℃ ... Ambient Temperature: 45 ℃' without justification

findings.reason: Section 4 introduces decision factor formula yj = (Tj − 2·Tmax)² (equation 10) to weight task assignment but provides no mathematical or physical justification for this parabolic relationship. Why squared? Why factor of 2 times Tmax? No derivation from thermal RC-model, optimization theory, or empirical validation. Figure 3 plots curve but does not explain principle.
findings.locator: Section 4 page 5, Equation (10) and Figure 3; no derivation provided for choice of quadratic form

findings.reason: Algorithm-1 specifies fixed iteration count 'For g=1 to iter' but no proof of convergence to global or local optimum, no analysis of computational complexity, no stopping criteria beyond iteration count. No comparison of fitness values across generations, no statistical analysis of solution quality, no validation that task assignment improves thermal balance beyond fitness function definition.
findings.locator: Section 4 Algorithm-1 page 7; Section 5.3 results report final temperatures but not genetic algorithm convergence history or fitness trajectory

findings.reason: Paper describes workflow: GEM5 → execution time, McPAT → power, then HotSpot → temperature, then Algorithm-1 → task assignment. But no documentation of data flow, file formats, parsing scripts, or integration code provided. How McPAT output (typically XML or tabular) maps to task power values in Table 1 unexplained. How HotSpot trace file feeds back as input to next hyper-period algorithm iteration not specified.
findings.locator: Section 3.2 Figure 1 page 4; Section 4 page 6-7; Section 5.1 page 7; no executable scripts or API documentation

findings.reason: Paper assumes core temperatures converge to steady-state within each hyper-period such that final temperature becomes initial condition for next period. No evidence provided: no convergence plots, no time-to-steady-state measurements, no verification that 10 hyper-periods of ~14 seconds simulation duration suffice for thermal equilibration. Transient peaks visible in Figures 7 and 9 suggest non-steady behavior.
findings.locator: Section 5.3 page 9: 'the final temperature of each hyper-period will be the initial temperature of the next hyper-period' stated without justification; Figures 7-10 show large transient oscillations

findings.reason: Results show maximum temperature difference of 8-9°C achieved by proposed genetic algorithm but no baseline heuristic provided (e.g., round-robin task assignment, random assignment, power-only balancing, temperature-unaware EDF). No comparison against prior work cited in introduction (Rubio-Anguiano et al., Rodriguez & Yomsi, Rupanetti & Salamy, Li et al., Jayaseelan & Mitra) to quantify improvement.
findings.locator: Section 6 Conclusion page 10 claims 'validate the effectiveness' but Section 5.3 results lack baseline comparison; Introduction pages 1-2 cites related work but no comparative evaluation

findings.reason: Abstract and Conclusion state 'highest temperature difference between the cores is 8 ℃ for approximately 14 seconds' but Section 5.3 runs '10 hyper-periods' of unspecified duration per period. If total simulation is 14 seconds and 10 hyper-periods, then ~1.4 seconds per hyper-period. But task execution times in Table 1 range from 62.553 ms to 882.386 ms; 10 parallel tasks could exceed 1.4 seconds. Duration calculation not provided.
findings.locator: Abstract page 1; Section 5.3 page 9 states '10 hyper-periods' without specifying duration per period; Section 6 page 10-11 references '14 seconds' without derivation

findings.reason: Figure 6 caption promises 'Simulation architecture consisting of a 4 cores CPU' but provides only abstract block diagram. No die dimensions (mm²), core area, core-to-core spacing, L2-cache location, memory controller placement, or thermal interface material (TIM) properties provided. These are essential inputs for HotSpot floorplan (.flp) file format.
findings.locator: Section 5.1 Figure 6 page 7; no coordinate or dimension data accessible

findings.reason: Section 6 Conclusion acknowledges 'there's a large peak takes place during each hyper-period' visible in Figures 7 and 9 but dismisses it as solvable via 'proper task portioning algorithm' without analyzing peak magnitude, cause, or impact on reliability. Peak-to-steady-state difference appears to exceed 8°C difference, contradicting main claim.
findings.locator: Section 6 Conclusion page 11: 'large peak takes place during each hyper-period of the cores this can be eliminated by using a proper task portioning algorithm' but peak magnitude and duration not quantified in results
